channel.title: Business Administration A · Study Podcast
channel.description: Two-host study episodes for Business Administration A (HSG, Autumn 2026): lectures, readings, models and exam practice.
channel.itunes:author: Adrián

item.title: Episode 6 · Innovation I · Lego, Ambidexterity and Growth
item.description: Lecture 5 of Business Administration A. VRIO and absorptive capacity, the Lego case from crisis to comeback, exploitation versus exploration, the three types of ambidexterity, multidexterity, the Ansoff matrix, diversification and performance, open innovation, and business model innovation. Quiz questions have pauses so you can answer.

item.title: Episode 5 · Strategy II · Resources and Capabilities
item.description: Lecture 4 of Business Administration A. Why profits differ within one industry, the market-based versus resource-based view, tangible and intangible resources, Porter's value chain, VRIN and the competitive analysis, the knowledge-based view and tacit knowledge, dynamic capabilities (sensing, seizing, reconfiguring), absorptive capacity, SWOT, and how much industry versus firm explains performance. Quiz questions have pauses so you can answer.

item.title: Episode 4 · Strategy I · Porter's Five Forces
item.description: Lecture 3 of Business Administration A. What strategy is and is not, Rumelt's core of good strategy, Porter's five forces with the conditions for each, the ASML example, PESTEL, M&A and the Bayer case, economic moats, Porter's generic strategies from the textbook, and why firms and regulators want opposite things. Quiz questions have pauses so you can answer.

item.title: Episode 3 · Alliances, Networks and Platforms
item.description: Lecture 2 of Business Administration A. Hybrid governance between market and hierarchy, types of alliances from consortia to M&A, how alliances are governed (contracts, trust, relational norms, termination rights), networks, and how digital platforms create value through network effects and intermediation. Quiz questions have pauses so you can answer.

item.title: Episode 2 · Why Do Firms Exist?
item.description: Lecture 1 (part 2) of Business Administration A. The economic problem, division of labour from Adam Smith to Ford and Taylor, transaction cost economics (Coase), make or buy, vertical integration at Tesla, asset specificity, uncertainty and frequency, the hold-up problem and its game-theory solution, and the five theories of the firm. Quiz questions have pauses so you can answer.

item.title: Episode 1 · Value Creation and the St. Gallen Management Model
item.description: Lecture 1 (part 1) and the week 1 reading of Business Administration A. How the course and exam work, what value creation means, the disciplines of business administration, the St. Gallen Management Model, and the three tools from the reading: locating a challenge, the causal chain, and from stakeholder to consequence. Quiz questions have pauses so you can answer.
